text:
Noah Dobson hasn't scored in 20 games this season, and he's not short of trying: 41 shots on goal and 3.0 expected goals (the quality of his chances), more than any season-opening stretch should produce nothing from. Montreal has also scored 5.4 fewer goals than its chances deserve with him on the ice. Both of those usually swing back.

In his second season in Montreal after the trade from the Islanders, he's playing 21 minutes a night and the Canadiens take 53% of the five-on-five expected goals with him out there, a little better than without him. That's an improvement on last season, when Evolving-Hockey had him in the bottom 5% of defensemen for chances allowed against top competition. His eight assists keep coming, including five in a four-game stretch around the turn of the month.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking flags the thing to watch: he shoots a lot, 81st percentile for attempts, but fewer from the slot than his volume suggests. Our talent range still has him around 7 goals for the year. The first one will come; how quickly may depend on whether he gets inside more often. With Mike Matheson hurt, his minutes should rise.
